titleBlock.headline: Inhibition of IL-11 signalling extends mammalian healthspan and lifespan
titleBlock.authors: Widjaja, A.A., Lim, W.-W., Viswanathan, S., Chothani, S., Corden, B., Dasan, C.M., Goh, J.W.T., Lim, R., Singh, B.K., Tan, J., Pua, C.J., Lim, S.Y., Adami, E., Schafer, S., Cook, S.A. et al.

researchSummary:
This is a summary of the scientific study.
Not affiliated with the study authors or their institutions.
whatIsIL11: Interleukin-11 (IL-11) is an IL-6 family cytokine. Once mischaracterized as anti-inflammatory or purely hematopoietic, it is now known to be a potent pro-fibrotic and pro-inflammatory factor signaling via IL-11RA and gp130.
Why does it matter for aging?

Across aged murine tissues (liver, visceral adipose, skeletal muscle, heart, kidney), IL-11 expression progressively rises inside senescent stromal, epithelial, and smooth muscle cells—hyperactivating ERK1/2 and mTORC1 while inhibiting AMPK.

Late-life monthly administration of a neutralizing anti-IL-11 antibody (X203, started at 75 weeks of age, ~55 human years) extended mouse median lifespan by 22.5% in males (130.3 to 159.6 weeks) and 25.0% in females (117.1 to 146.4 weeks; +28.7% pooled, p < 0.0001), while germline Il11-/- deletion extended pooled median lifespan by 24.9% (120.9 to 151.0 weeks, p < 0.0001) and slashed age-related cancer deaths.

studyOverview.label: Objective
studyOverview.value: Test whether genetic deletion or late-life pharmacological neutralization of IL-11 signaling extends mammalian healthspan and lifespan.

studyOverview.label: Design
studyOverview.value: Germline Il11ra1/Il11 KO cohorts + late-life monthly anti-IL-11 mAb (X203, 40 mg/kg) from 75 weeks of age in male and female C57BL/6J mice.

studyOverview.label: Lifespan Result
studyOverview.value: +22.5% median lifespan in males, +25.0% in females (+28.7% pooled, p < 0.0001) with anti-IL-11 mAb; +24.9% pooled in Il11-/- knockout mice.

studyOverview.label: Healthspan Result
studyOverview.value: Reversed sarcopenia & frailty, prevented brown-to-white fat conversion, preserved telomeres/mitochondria, and reduced macroscopic tumors (~16% vs >60% at autopsy).

scorecardOverview.title: The Question
scorecardOverview.content: Does progressive age-related upregulation of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-11 causally drive mammalian multimorbidity and mortality—and can late-life antibody blockade reverse it?

scorecardOverview.title: The Methodology
scorecardOverview.content: Evaluated aging biomarkers, metabolism, fibrosis, and full survival curves in Il11ra1-/- and Il11-/- knockout mice, and administered an anti-IL-11 neutralizing antibody (X203, 40 mg/kg) monthly to 75-week-old C57BL/6J mice (~55 human years) until natural death.

scorecardOverview.title: The Breakthrough
scorecardOverview.content: Late-life anti-IL-11 therapy extended median lifespan by 22.5% in males and 25.0% in females (+28.7% pooled; matching +24.9% in germline Il11-/- knockouts), restored AMPK activity while suppressing ERK/mTORC1, preserved lean muscle strength, and markedly lowered age-related neoplasia.

mechanismDescription: Age-induced IL-11 upregulation acts as a master feed-forward switch: binding to IL-11RA/gp130 activates MEK/ERK1/2, which phosphorylates and inactivates LKB1/AMPK, releasing the brake on mTORC1 and canonical JAK/STAT3 inflammaging.

pathwaySteps.desc: Senescent and damaged cells in liver, fat, and muscle chronically secrete IL-11 after middle age.
Autocrine and paracrine binding to IL-11RA/gp130 triggers non-canonical MEK/ERK and canonical JAK/STAT3.
ERK1/2 inactivates LKB1/AMPK, causing persistent mTORC1 hyperactivation and impaired autophagy.
Drives p16/p21 senescence amplification, tissue fibrosis, visceral adiposity, sarcopenia, and tumorigenesis.

keyFindings.title: Sex-Robust Lifespan Extension
keyFindings.desc: Unlike many longevity drugs that show strong sex dimorphism, monthly anti-IL-11 therapy from 75 weeks of age extended median lifespan by 22.5% in males (130.3 to 159.6 weeks) and 25.0% in females (117.1 to 146.4 weeks; +28.7% pooled, p < 0.0001), while germline Il11-/- deletion extended pooled median lifespan by 24.9% (p < 0.0001).

keyFindings.title: Reversal of Sarcopenia & Frailty
keyFindings.desc: Treated aged mice showed 2.5-fold smaller visceral white adipose (vWAT) lipid droplet area, significantly lower clinical frailty index scores, preserved four-limb grip strength, and reduced skeletal muscle and cardiac fibrosis.

keyFindings.title: Metabolic & Thermogenic Rejuvenation
keyFindings.desc: Anti-IL-11 prevented age-related visceral fat expansion, restored uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) thermogenesis and 'beiging' in subcutaneous adipose tissue, and normalized glucose tolerance.

keyFindings.title: Suppression of Senescence & Tumors
keyFindings.desc: Neutralizing IL-11 broke the autocrine SASP amplification loop (lowering p16Ink4a, p21Cip1, and serum IL-6) and reduced macroscopic tumors at gross necropsy from >60% in IgG controls to ~16%.

conclusions: IL-11 is a fundamental, targetable upstream driver of the ERK–AMPK–mTORC1 aging cascade in mammals.

Late-life pharmacological blockade of IL-11 extends both male (+22.5%) and female (+25.0%; +28.7% pooled) median lifespan—and germline Il11-/- deletion extends pooled median lifespan by +24.9%—while compressing late-life frailty and tumor burden.
Humanized anti-IL-11 and anti-IL-11RA antibodies already in Phase 1/2 fibrotic disease trials offer a near-term translational path for human multimorbidity.

structuredConclusions.title: Upstream Convergence on AMPK & mTORC1
structuredConclusions.content: Blocking extracellular IL-11 simultaneously restores LKB1/AMPK activity and dampens mTORC1—combining the intracellular benefits of metformin and rapamycin without immunosuppressive toxicity.

structuredConclusions.title: Robust Late-Life Efficacy in Both Sexes
structuredConclusions.content: Initiating monthly anti-IL-11 antibody treatment at 75 weeks of age (~55 human years) extended median lifespan by +22.5% in males and +25.0% in females (+28.7% pooled, p < 0.0001), closely paralleling lifelong germline Il11-/- deletion (+24.9% pooled).

structuredConclusions.title: Simultaneous Anti-Fibrotic & Anti-Cancer Action
structuredConclusions.content: Beyond preserving muscle mass, metabolic flexibility, and telomere length, IL-11 neutralization reduced age-related macroscopic tumor incidence at autopsy from over 60% in controls to ~16%.

protocolRecommendations: Humanized anti-IL-11/IL-11RA monoclonal antibodies (such as BI 765423 and LASN01) are currently in human clinical trials for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and fibro-inflammatory diseases, representing a major translational candidate to watch.

Because IL-11 exerts its pro-aging effects by inhibiting LKB1/AMPK and hyperactivating ERK/mTORC1, accessible interventions that directly activate AMPK and restrain mTORC1 (aerobic exercise, caloric moderation, and senomorphic polyphenols) target the exact downstream node.
